Rubens, Ensor and other great artists in a splendid temple for the arts.","relevance":"medium","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[KMSKA, a renovated temple for the arts without equal > Old Masters]

Such great art belongs in a monumental location. The **Rubens and Van Dyck Halls** in the KMSKA are more than up to the task. In the hall, which is no less than 15 metres high, Rubens’ altarpieces such as The Adoration of the Magi and The Baptism of Christ hang in dialogue with those of other grandmasters like **Jacob Jordaens** and **Anthony van Dyck**. It makes a person feel small and insignificant, coming face to face with all these monumental masterpieces.

[KMSKA, a renovated temple for the arts without equal > Modernists]

The old masters are outstandingly represented here, but the more youthful greats are illustrated superbly as well. This is demonstrated by the museum in the snow-white Ensor Wing, dedicated to modern art pioneer James Ensor. Indeed, KMSKA has the world’s largest Ensor collection. Spread over two halls you will find, among other things, The Oyster Eater, Adam and Eve Expelled from Paradise and The Intrigue. Among these three milestones in his oeuvre you will also see numerous **still lifes, early bourgeois salons and late seascapes**. These are complemented by four cabinets that showcase the other facets of this remarkable body of work.

…

[KMSKA, a renovated temple for the arts without equal > A splendid renovation]

In 2011, the museum closed its doors for a total restoration and expansion. A large internal depot was built, as was a new vertical structure that considerably increased the volume of the museum. The grandeur of the historic halls was reinstated. The friezes, busts, medallions and other sculptures in the museum were restored to their full glory. A new state-of-the-art climate system was installed. A brand-new museum garden was created. The scenography was completely rethought. In the end, this tour de force took 11 years. But the result is more than worth it.

…

Today, the Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp is **one of the most important ambassadors in the Flemish arts landscape**. In the halls of the KMSKA you can admire no fewer than 640 works of art, supplemented by temporary exhibitions. So if you come back to Antwerp, make time to admire all this beauty. You won’t regret it."],"code":"SUCCESS"}},{"url":"https://www.visitflanders.com/en/flemish-destinations/antwerp?country=en_US","title":"Visit Flanders – Antwerp","description":"Its Grote Markt and cathedral, ... Plantin-Moretus Museum, Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA), the Museum of Contemporary Art Antwerp (M HKA) and much more…...","relevance":"medium","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[Antwerp > Antwerp, Stylish to a Fault]

Business travellers, artists, fashionistas and diamond merchants; all can still be found here. Antwerp combines the grandeur of yesteryear with an urban vibrancy. Its Grote Markt and cathedral, Scheldt riverbanks and cobbled streets go hand in hand with a thriving nightlife, galleries and art palaces. It is home to the Rubens House, Plantin-Moretus Museum, Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA), the Museum of Contemporary Art Antwerp (M HKA) and much more… The options in Antwerp are endless, as long as they have that gleam.

…

[Antwerp > Museum Plantin-Moretus will reopen on Saturday 5 December]

Museum Plantin-Moretus is temporarily closed for renovations. During this time, work is being done on an updated visitor route, a new exhibition design and a visitor app. These renovations will make the story of the printing house and the Plantin-Moretus family even more accessible to the general public. Museum Plantin-Moretus will reopen on Saturday 5 December.

…

[Antwerp > 48 hours in Antwerp, a splendid experience]

Time speeds by when you’re in Antwerp. There is so much to experience here, from Baroque master Peter Paul Rubens’s artistic legacy, the Railway Cathedral, the port that is this city’s lifeblood, ground-breaking fashion, sparkling diamonds and much, much more. Prepare yourself for 48 hours in Antwerp."],"code":"SUCCESS"}},{"url":"https://www.visitflanders.com/en/discover-flanders/arts-and-heritage/flemish-masters","title":"Flemish Masters of Art | VISITFLANDERS","description":"You can discover their impressive legacy in Flanders' most prominent museums, such as the Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA), the Museum of Fine Arts Ghent (MSK) and the Groeninge Museum Bruges.","relevance":"medium","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[Flemish Masters]

You can discover their impressive legacy in Flanders' most prominent museums, such as the Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA), the Museum of Fine Arts Ghent (MSK) and the Groeninge Museum Bruges. Although their work can equally be found in churches, castles, town halls, abbeys, chapels or in the artists' homes. These were the places where the Flemish Masters lived and worked and where they found the inspiration for their masterpieces.

…

[Flemish Masters > More about the Flemish Masters > KMSKA, a renovated temple for the arts without equal]

The KMSKA, the Royal Museum of Fine Arts in Antwerp, welcomes you with open arms. Rubens, Ensor and other great artists in a splendid temple for the arts."],"code":"SUCCESS"}},{"url":"https://www.visitflanders.com/en/inspiring-itineraries/48-hours-antwerp-grandiose-experience","title":"48 hours in Antwerp, a grandiose experience | VISITFLANDERS","description":"And what an encounter it is: the Royal Museum of Fine Arts in Antwerp (KMSKA).This splendid museum finally reopened its doors at the end of 2022, after a comprehensive and detailed renovation that lasted an impressive 11 years.","relevance":"medium","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[48 hours in Antwerp, a splendid experience > Day 1 > Cutting-edge fashion]

This fashion quarter confirms that Antwerp stands for new, cutting-edge designs. The same applies to the arts. For proof, see the Museum of Contemporary Art Antwerp (**M HKA**, housed in a former grain silo. Enter a dark labyrinth on the museum’s ground floor to discover thought-inspiring artwork by contemporary greats such as Luc Tuymans, Guillaume Bijl and artist and visionary Panamarenko. On the other floors, temporary exhibitions offer further challenges.

…

[48 hours in Antwerp, a splendid experience > Day 2 > Rubens, part 2]

All good things come in threes, or so the saying goes. So, we will add a third Rubens encounter. And what an encounter it is: the Royal Museum of Fine Arts in Antwerp (**KMSKA**).This splendid museum finally reopened its doors at the end of 2022, after a comprehensive and detailed renovation that lasted an impressive 11 years. This palace of the arts is home to a staggering collection of over 13,000 pieces. Among them are works by many great historic European painters. Antwerp’s leading artistic icon takes pride of place, of course. KMSKA’s breathtaking Rubens Hall contains sixteen of his paintings, including such masterpieces as his Adoration of the Magi and Venus Frigida. The museum also holds the world’s largest collection of works by modern master James Ensor in addition to masterpieces by Jan van Eyck, Hans Memling, Jean Fouquet, Amedeo Modigliani, Pierre Alechinsky and many, oh so many more."],"code":"SUCCESS"}},{"url":"https://www.visitflanders.com/en/travel-information/accessibility/accessible-heritage-flanders","title":"Accessible heritage in Flanders | VISITFLANDERS","description":"From Flemish Masters in situ, to museums including KMSKA in Antwerp, M Museum in Leuven and The Mystic Lamb in St. Bavo's Cathedral in Ghent: Flanders is about heritage, and it lives and breathes art. We want to share it with everyone.","relevance":"medium","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[Accessible heritage in Flanders > Accessible museums and attractions]

From KMSKA in Antwerp to M Museum in Leuven, the Mystic Lamb in St. Bavo's Cathedral in Ghent, and the Church of Our Lady in Bruges. Here you will find not only world-class masterpieces, but also a comfortable and hassle-free visit for all. Thanks to **accessible entrances, lifts, wheelchair-friendly routes, assistance aids and adapted tours**, you can experience these temples of art at your pace.

[Accessible heritage in Flanders > Royal Museum of Fine Arts, Antwerp]

From the Flemish Primitives to the Expressionists, KSMKA is the home of 7 centuries of art excellence. Masterpieces by Peter Paul Rubens and James Ensor, among others, will leave you in awe. The KMSKA app also offers the room texts in Flemish Sign Language and International Sign. The museum organises customised tours for blind, visually impaired, deaf and hard of hearing visitors. People with autism or dementia can use special formulas to explore the museum. The recently renovated building is suitable for wheelchairs on all floors, and you will find gender-neutral and accessible toilets throughout. There are adapted parking spaces nearby for people with disabilities.

…

[Accessible heritage in Flanders > Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium, Brussels]

The Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium (KMSKB) are a collection of world-class museums in bustling Brussels. Discover the superb art collection from the 15th century to the present day, with masterpieces by Bruegel, Rubens and Ensor, among others. There is an alternate **accessible entrance** for visitors with physical disabilities. There are adapted **parking spaces** for people with reduced mobility. The 'Made to Measure' programme allows deaf, hard of hearing, blind and visually impaired visitors and people with mental or physical disabilities to experience art through **guided tours**."],"code":"SUCCESS"}},{"url":"https://www.visitflanders.com/en/discover-flanders/arts-and-heritage/flemish-masters/james-ensor","title":"James Ensor, North Sea Pioneer | VISITFLANDERS","description":"The Royal Museum of Fine Arts in Antwerp (KMSKA) has the largest Ensor collection in the world and the Royal Museums of Fine Arts in Brussels (KMSKB) have a fair amount of his work on display.","relevance":"medium","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[James Ensor > James Ensor, North Sea pioneer]

The Queen of seaside resorts remains this grand master’s home to this day. His residence for the last 30 years of his life has been renamed Ensor House and is now a unique piece of heritage with a splendid visitor centre. Nearby Mu.ZEE grants an additional glimpse into his life and work.

Much of his rich body of work has also found its way into major museums around the world. Still, Flanders offers the best introduction to his greatness. The Royal Museum of Fine Arts in Antwerp (KMSKA) has the largest Ensor collection in the world and the Royal Museums of Fine Arts in Brussels (KMSKB) have a fair amount of his work on display. The museums Plantin-Moretus (Museum Plantin-Moretus is currently closed for renovations and will reopen on Saturday 5 December) Dhondt-Dhaenens and the Museum of Fine Arts (MSK) in Ghent have also continued to spread his message to the world.

…

[James Ensor > Ensor in Flanders > Peter Paul Rubens]

This master of the Baroque is Antwerp through and through. Discover Peter Paul Rubens' masterly works at the Rubenshuis, the KMSKA or in the city's Cathedral."],"code":"SUCCESS"}},{"url":"https://www.visitflanders.com/sites/visitflanders/files/public/media/files/2025-12/2026%20Events%20in%20Flanders_1.pdf","title":"Note: Press CTL + click subheading below to go to entry.","description":"The Roger Raveel Museum is closed for renovations. Reopening scheduled for June 28, 2026. http://rogerraveelmuseum.be/en/news/tijdelijke-sluiting ... Mu.ZEE is closed until 2028 for major renovations.","relevance":"medium","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[Ongoing events The Antwerp Six EXHIBITION MoMu Antwerp]

title
ntony Gormley Geestgrond
EXHIBITION
KMSKA, Antwerp
23 May 2026 – 20 September 2026
Antony Gormley. Geestgrond is the first major presentation of the celebrated artist in Belgium,
created specially for the spaces of KMSKA. Bringing together early works, well known bodycase
sculptures and recent spatial installations, the exhibition explores the human body as a source
of experience and connection, with newer pieces portraying people as transparent and
delicately linked to their surroundings. Works from the museums historical collection are shown
alongside Gormleys sculptures, turning KMSKA into a place where old and new meet.

…

Jenny Montigny
EXHIBITION
MSK, Ghent
10 October 2026 – 10 January 2027
In the autumn of 2026, the Museum of Fine Arts in Ghent celebrates the Ghent-born artist Jenny
Montigny (1875-1937). More than a century after her first retrospective in 1922, the museum
presents a wide selection of her works, drawn from its own collection as well as from public
and private loans.

…

Ostend
Mu.ZEE is closed until 2028 for major renovations. In the meantime, the museum's collection is
traveling to the Venetian Galleries in Ostend and beyond!"],"code":"SUCCESS"}}],"query":"site:visitflanders.com art museums KMSKA MSK Mu.ZEE M HKA","cache_metadata":{"status":"miss","age_ms":0},"request_id":"1fe31149-0e23-4edb-9213-5dbe9c946f17"}

A new state-of-the-art climate system was installed. A brand-new museum garden was created. The scenography was completely rethought. In the end, this tour de force took 11 years. But the result is more than worth it.

…

Today, the Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp is **one of the most important ambassadors in the Flemish arts landscape**. In the halls of the KMSKA you can admire no fewer than 640 works of art, supplemented by temporary exhibitions. So if you come back to Antwerp, make time to admire all this beauty. You won’t regret it.

results.description: Its Grote Markt and cathedral, ... Plantin-Moretus Museum, Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA), the Museum of Contemporary Art Antwerp (M HKA) and much more…...

highlights:
[Antwerp > Antwerp, Stylish to a Fault]

Business travellers, artists, fashionistas and diamond merchants; all can still be found here. Antwerp combines the grandeur of yesteryear with an urban vibrancy. Its Grote Markt and cathedral, Scheldt riverbanks and cobbled streets go hand in hand with a thriving nightlife, galleries and art palaces. It is home to the Rubens House, Plantin-Moretus Museum, Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA), the Museum of Contemporary Art Antwerp (M HKA) and much more… The options in Antwerp are endless, as long as they have that gleam.

…

[Antwerp > Museum Plantin-Moretus will reopen on Saturday 5 December]

Museum Plantin-Moretus is temporarily closed for renovations. During this time, work is being done on an updated visitor route, a new exhibition design and a visitor app. These renovations will make the story of the printing house and the Plantin-Moretus family even more accessible to the general public. Museum Plantin-Moretus will reopen on Saturday 5 December.

…

[Antwerp > 48 hours in Antwerp, a splendid experience]

Time speeds by when you’re in Antwerp. There is so much to experience here, from Baroque master Peter Paul Rubens’s artistic legacy, the Railway Cathedral, the port that is this city’s lifeblood, ground-breaking fashion, sparkling diamonds and much, much more. Prepare yourself for 48 hours in Antwerp.

highlights:
[Flemish Masters]

You can discover their impressive legacy in Flanders' most prominent museums, such as the Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA), the Museum of Fine Arts Ghent (MSK) and the Groeninge Museum Bruges. Although their work can equally be found in churches, castles, town halls, abbeys, chapels or in the artists' homes. These were the places where the Flemish Masters lived and worked and where they found the inspiration for their masterpieces.

…

[Flemish Masters > More about the Flemish Masters > KMSKA, a renovated temple for the arts without equal]

The KMSKA, the Royal Museum of Fine Arts in Antwerp, welcomes you with open arms. Rubens, Ensor and other great artists in a splendid temple for the arts.

results.title: 48 hours in Antwerp, a grandiose experience | VISITFLANDERS
results.description: And what an encounter it is: the Royal Museum of Fine Arts in Antwerp (KMSKA).This splendid museum finally reopened its doors at the end of 2022, after a comprehensive and detailed renovation that lasted an impressive 11 years.

highlights:
[48 hours in Antwerp, a splendid experience > Day 1 > Cutting-edge fashion]

This fashion quarter confirms that Antwerp stands for new, cutting-edge designs. The same applies to the arts. For proof, see the Museum of Contemporary Art Antwerp (**M HKA**, housed in a former grain silo. Enter a dark labyrinth on the museum’s ground floor to discover thought-inspiring artwork by contemporary greats such as Luc Tuymans, Guillaume Bijl and artist and visionary Panamarenko. On the other floors, temporary exhibitions offer further challenges.

…

[48 hours in Antwerp, a splendid experience > Day 2 > Rubens, part 2]

All good things come in threes, or so the saying goes. So, we will add a third Rubens encounter. And what an encounter it is: the Royal Museum of Fine Arts in Antwerp (**KMSKA**).This splendid museum finally reopened its doors at the end of 2022, after a comprehensive and detailed renovation that lasted an impressive 11 years. This palace of the arts is home to a staggering collection of over 13,000 pieces. Among them are works by many great historic European painters. Antwerp’s leading artistic icon takes pride of place, of course. KMSKA’s breathtaking Rubens Hall contains sixteen of his paintings, including such masterpieces as his Adoration of the Magi and Venus Frigida. The museum also holds the world’s largest collection of works by modern master James Ensor in addition to masterpieces by Jan van Eyck, Hans Memling, Jean Fouquet, Amedeo Modigliani, Pierre Alechinsky and many, oh so many more.

results.title: Accessible heritage in Flanders | VISITFLANDERS
results.description: From Flemish Masters in situ, to museums including KMSKA in Antwerp, M Museum in Leuven and The Mystic Lamb in St. Bavo's Cathedral in Ghent: Flanders is about heritage, and it lives and breathes art. We want to share it with everyone.

highlights:
[Accessible heritage in Flanders > Accessible museums and attractions]

From KMSKA in Antwerp to M Museum in Leuven, the Mystic Lamb in St. Bavo's Cathedral in Ghent, and the Church of Our Lady in Bruges. Here you will find not only world-class masterpieces, but also a comfortable and hassle-free visit for all. Thanks to **accessible entrances, lifts, wheelchair-friendly routes, assistance aids and adapted tours**, you can experience these temples of art at your pace.

[Accessible heritage in Flanders > Royal Museum of Fine Arts, Antwerp]

From the Flemish Primitives to the Expressionists, KSMKA is the home of 7 centuries of art excellence. Masterpieces by Peter Paul Rubens and James Ensor, among others, will leave you in awe. The KMSKA app also offers the room texts in Flemish Sign Language and International Sign. The museum organises customised tours for blind, visually impaired, deaf and hard of hearing visitors. People with autism or dementia can use special formulas to explore the museum. The recently renovated building is suitable for wheelchairs on all floors, and you will find gender-neutral and accessible toilets throughout. There are adapted parking spaces nearby for people with disabilities.

…

[Accessible heritage in Flanders > Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium, Brussels]

The Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium (KMSKB) are a collection of world-class museums in bustling Brussels. Discover the superb art collection from the 15th century to the present day, with masterpieces by Bruegel, Rubens and Ensor, among others. There is an alternate **accessible entrance** for visitors with physical disabilities. There are adapted **parking spaces** for people with reduced mobility. The 'Made to Measure' programme allows deaf, hard of hearing, blind and visually impaired visitors and people with mental or physical disabilities to experience art through **guided tours**.

results.title: James Ensor, North Sea Pioneer | VISITFLANDERS
results.description: The Royal Museum of Fine Arts in Antwerp (KMSKA) has the largest Ensor collection in the world and the Royal Museums of Fine Arts in Brussels (KMSKB) have a fair amount of his work on display.

highlights:
[James Ensor > James Ensor, North Sea pioneer]

The Queen of seaside resorts remains this grand master’s home to this day. His residence for the last 30 years of his life has been renamed Ensor House and is now a unique piece of heritage with a splendid visitor centre. Nearby Mu.ZEE grants an additional glimpse into his life and work.

Much of his rich body of work has also found its way into major museums around the world. Still, Flanders offers the best introduction to his greatness. The Royal Museum of Fine Arts in Antwerp (KMSKA) has the largest Ensor collection in the world and the Royal Museums of Fine Arts in Brussels (KMSKB) have a fair amount of his work on display. The museums Plantin-Moretus (Museum Plantin-Moretus is currently closed for renovations and will reopen on Saturday 5 December) Dhondt-Dhaenens and the Museum of Fine Arts (MSK) in Ghent have also continued to spread his message to the world.

…

[James Ensor > Ensor in Flanders > Peter Paul Rubens]

This master of the Baroque is Antwerp through and through. Discover Peter Paul Rubens' masterly works at the Rubenshuis, the KMSKA or in the city's Cathedral.

ntony Gormley Geestgrond
EXHIBITION
KMSKA, Antwerp
23 May 2026 – 20 September 2026
Antony Gormley. Geestgrond is the first major presentation of the celebrated artist in Belgium,
created specially for the spaces of KMSKA. Bringing together early works, well known bodycase
sculptures and recent spatial installations, the exhibition explores the human body as a source
of experience and connection, with newer pieces portraying people as transparent and
delicately linked to their surroundings. Works from the museums historical collection are shown
alongside Gormleys sculptures, turning KMSKA into a place where old and new meet.

In the autumn of 2026, the Museum of Fine Arts in Ghent celebrates the Ghent-born artist Jenny
Montigny (1875-1937). More than a century after her first retrospective in 1922, the museum
presents a wide selection of her works, drawn from its own collection as well as from public
and private loans.
